in_question.sentence: Most rooms were standing communities before the canvas opened, with their own subject and rules, and the canvas arrived as a flood of posts about something else.
Moderation or gatekeeping as such: removals belong here only when they draw the line between the sub's business and the event.
In-group humour, or culture as such: the construct holds only the traffic between a frame the room had and the new episode.
Each account could place one pixel per interval, and no one could order another to place.
The form pass found such lines and never counted them.
Here no one could hold a member's time or assign it.

The calls here rarely offer anything beyond the work: a reward offered before the work appears in 9 of 705 rooms (F-016), for example 'As an insentive, for every person who joins in and comments below I will post 5 pig gifs!

In six rooms or fewer each, they adopt a sign others began, make a tribute alone, build memorials to the dead, leave the work unsigned, plan a mark that moves in the timelapse or follow the creator's wishes. 483 of 705 rooms carry at least one of these: 'Does it bother anyone else that the logo is off center.....' [smite/c0348].
The record does not show whether placers who never wrote followed the canvas.
Here any member may post a template (Standardization of output, 237 rooms), and no one can make placers follow it.
Here anyone may post a template, and no one can make a placer follow it.
A template here is posted for anyone to follow, and no one can order a placer to follow it.
Here the workaround evades the rate limit that applies to every account, and members in 80 rooms argue whether scripts are fair.
They announce in the thread what the chat decided (33 rooms): 'Over in the discord we've decided not to expand south any farther.' [dwarffortress/c0079].
What a chat decided reaches the record only when a member brings it back to the thread.
The form pass, which counted nothing, found the question who leads almost never asked.
Here a decided leader or vote binds no placer who does not choose to follow, since no one can order another to place.
Anyone could change any pixel.

They defend it against attackers (392 rooms), watch it and repair changed pixels (293), choose upkeep over expansion (43), concentrate effort on fewer pieces (29), cover the night shift (24) and reshape the mark against tampering (20): 'Remember to maintain, not just expand!' [greenlattice/c0215]. 526 of 705 rooms carry at least one of these, gated on the rooms with a work of their own.

In seven rooms or fewer each, hosts vet others' requests to build, members dispute who may approve a spot, and a room relies on a bigger neighbour. 288 of 705 rooms carry at least one of these: 'Well, we were here first.
Property rights or possession: nothing here is owned, only claimed.

Two rooms or fewer each defy the call for restraint, mourn art the room covered, place rival marks together or urge repair over retaliation. 205 of 705 rooms carry at least one of these: 'We mean you no harm!

In six rooms or fewer each, a room stays neutral, members negotiate across a language gap, argue whether cooperation is surrender or trade away another room's work. 467 of 705 rooms carry at least one of these.

Members say themselves that an agreement does not bind every placer: 'Their group has agreed to not mess with our space but there will always be those individuals who don't listen / care' [hentai/c0105].

Members form alliances between rooms (91 rooms), meet other rooms in a chat (31), make joint marks (27), gather kindred rooms in a hub (13) and tally kindred rooms' works (6): 'Hi all - trying to help with team logos. /r/nbaplace has been created to coordinate different team subs' [lakers/c0155]. 146 of 705 rooms carry at least one of these.
Members work out who changed their work and why.
In three rooms or fewer each, members plant disguised scripts on rivals, brigade one person off Reddit or relay a streamer's call to attack. 231 of 705 rooms carry at least one of these.

In some rooms, a tie from before the canvas names the rival in the same turn as the attack (C02, untested for order; F-013: 10 turns in 7 story rooms), and membership carried in does not come before the attack more often than chance (F-011).

In five rooms or fewer each, they weigh the room against nations, dispute national belonging, debate friendship with historic enemies or argue the nation's historical record. 62 of 705 rooms carry at least one of these: 'We did it again after 1965 and 1971, now at r/Place.' [pakistan/c0240].
Membership carried in does not come before the attack more often than chance (F-011).
Anyone could place any pixel.
The theme was never tested as an element; at pass 5 it was the residue of six story rooms.
Coined, this corpus's: nothing was borrowed to change.
It names the set of ways a room aligned many hands on one picture when no one could give an order that bound anyone.
Defence is one act inside it; resilience names an outcome, the work surviving, which this study reads from the record and never from the canvas.
There is no common pool to manage here, only adjacent works.
Membership carried in does not come before the attack more often than chance (F-011).
The emblem is what the room chooses to show; identity is the membership the work carries, which can exist before any emblem is chosen.
Frame analysis would cover every interpretation in the corpus; this names only the host community's handling of its own space during the event.
Most rooms existed before the canvas; 78 of 705 have no posts in the week before it.
